name: Use the canonical catalog language from the context documents
description: The domain terms live in CONTEXT-MAP.md (the contexts and how they relate) and docs/contexts/<context>/CONTEXT.md (one glossary per context). Catalog and Inventory are written; others are added when their first seed starts. Use these terms exactly in code, docs and the UI, and check the glossary before adding a term. Keep the files current with the domain-modeling skill (~/.agents/skills/domain-modeling): a CONTEXT.md is only a glossary, with 1–2 sentence definitions and an Avoid list. docs/PRODUCT_PLAN.md was never committed and is unavailable.

title: Save every change to part details as a new, complete revision
rationale: Each change to part details saves a new, complete revision that never changes afterwards, grouped in a Change with a reason. Commands carry the current revision they expect. Restoring adds a new revision, and a change that alters nothing is rejected. Supplier data, stock, scans and drafts never create revisions.

title: Keep a CAD item's identity, its stored bytes and its revisions separate
rationale: A CAD item keeps its identity over time. Its stored bytes are identified by their SHA-256, and each revision's hash covers its content and license. Source and license belong to one exact CAD item revision. Moving or copying stored bytes never creates a revision.

title: Keep verification and protection separate
rationale: Verification is permanent proof about one exact revision. Protection is an audited setting that blocks changes to a part or CAD item. To fix a protected item, remove the protection with a reason, revise it, verify the new revision, then protect it again. Authority is never a silent way around protection.

name: Binary-safe content addressing inside PocketBase hooks
description: $security.sha256 hashes text, so bytes that are not UTF-8 would hash wrongly. The catalog import sends blobs as base64 in the JSON command and infra/pocketbase/pb_hooks/catalog_lib.js decodes and hashes them in pure JS before $filesystem.fileFromBytes, so blobs are verified and written in the same transaction; tooling/catalog-import test the_route_hashes_blob_bytes_exactly checks it against Rust's sha2 at 1, 55, 56, 63, 64, 119, 120 and 300,000 bytes (PocketBase cannot store an empty file, so the route refuses empty blobs). Canonical documents whose SHA-256 is their identity (snapshots, declarations) are stored in text fields with an explicit max (a TextField max of 0 means 5000), never json fields, so the hashed bytes round-trip. Shared hook code lives in a non-.pb.js file loaded with require(`${__hooks}/catalog_lib.js`) inside the handler.

title: Derive Catalog record IDs from content and diff legacy imports server-side
rationale: Every Catalog record ID is the first 15 hex digits of SHA-256('kicad-parts:<kind>:v1\n<key>') (Managed Part from IPN, Asset from kind+LIB:NAME, Asset Revision from asset+revision hash, Blob from bytes hash, Change Set from correlation ID), computed in crates/catalog/src/ids.rs and re-derived by the route, so re-imports resolve to the same records without a mapping table. A symbol's Asset Blob is the exact byte span of that one top-level symbol (Provenance keeps file path, file hash and byte range), so editing a neighbouring symbol does not revise it; footprints and 3D models are whole files. POST /api/catalog/legacy-imports diffs against stored state in one transaction: nothing new is a 422 no-op with no Change Set; a changed snapshot gets a successor only when the head's Change Set kind is legacy-import, otherwise an Import Diagnostic; a changed row with an unchanged snapshot (an Operational Fact) is kept as an Import Diagnostic. Supplier PNs, LCSC and prices stay in Part Revision Provenance, never in the snapshot.
